newsitem.title: UK: LCE cocoa futures end down, await Man crop data.
newsitem.headline: LCE cocoa futures end down, await Man crop data.

text.p: Cocoa futures ended with slight losses after an extremely quiet session, lacking fresh incentives and ahead of key crop data by UK trade house E D and F Man due later this week.
Traders said the market showed little reaction to forecasts of deficits for the 1996/97 crop by the International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) and UK firm Landell Mills.
By the close, the second-position December had fallen four stg to 976 stg a tonne after ranging between 973 and 981. Most-active March shed five to 995 stg.
Overall volume was a small 1,785 lots.
One trader said the Man report could show estimates of between 150,000 and 180,000 tonnes shortfall for the 1996/97 world cocoa balance.
On Tuesday, Landell Mills put the cocoa deficit at 150,000 tonnes while on Monday, the ICCO pegged the deficit at 225,000 tonnes.
"There is quite a spread of forecasts," said one trader.
Technically they said the market would remain pressured because on the forwards there is a big long position.
"But there is still a group who want to lobby the market higher," said one.
Adrian Haylor, technical analyst at Sucden, said cocoa could still move higher to the 990/1,000 stg a tonne territory, basis December, once the current consolidation phase is completed.
